enlighten

in-LY-tun -- three syllables, stress on the second syllable, LY. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To enlighten is to inform or give insight.

A single chat with the beekeeper can enlighten you about everything happening inside the hive.

Example

For years, Jamal has confidently called spiders insects. His little sister enlightens him by sliding her field notebook across the table: 'Count the legs -- eight, not six. Different body parts, too.' He stares, counts, and finally says, 'Huh. I had that completely wrong.'

She gave him new understanding that corrected what he thought he knew. Enlighten always turns a light on in the dark -- someone was ignorant or mistaken about something, and now they see it clearly.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

educate: To educate is to build someone's knowledge step by step over months and years, the way a school does. To enlighten works in a moment: one explanation switches the light on, correcting something a person had wrong or had never grasped.

instruct: To instruct is to teach a skill or direct someone in how to do something -- how to tie a knot, how to file a report. To enlighten changes understanding instead: it clears away ignorance or a mistaken belief rather than training a hand.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

confuse: to make something harder to understand

mislead: to give someone a false idea

Where it sits · how deeply it changes your understanding — inform → enlighten → illuminate

inform vs. enlighten: Inform just delivers the facts -- a schedule change informs you -- while enlighten goes deeper: the new information changes how you understand something you had wrong or never grasped.

illuminate vs. enlighten: Illuminate is the strongest and most vivid: to enlighten someone is to switch a light on for them, but an explanation that illuminates a whole subject leaves every corner of it glowing.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — en-

prefix — en-: to make, to put into (Latin in-, via French)

root — light

root — light: light, brightness (Old English leoht)

suffix — -en

suffix — -en: verb-forming, to cause (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Enlighten is literally 'to put light into' -- en- ('make, put into') plus light. Ignorance is pictured as darkness, so to enlighten someone is to bring a lamp into the dark room of what they did not know and let them finally see it.

Use the root in a new word: spotlight

Root Check

Word Choice

Enlighten corrects ignorance: it takes someone who did not know -- or had it wrong -- and gives them real insight, often with about ('enlighten voters about the new law'). Keep it apart from its cluster neighbors in this unit: impart hands over specific knowledge, and instill slowly builds character traits. A related word-family note: you met the adjective enlightening earlier in this course -- an enlightening lecture is simply one that enlightens you.
